clue.text: Star workers are inside

indicators.note: something inside sits within something else, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribute to the people who shine at a company: the staff are the real stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' looks like the staff of the surface, but in crosswords it is nearly always insects from the colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the bright red giant star at the heart of the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: Assistant in Dubai deli

indicators.note: the letters needed sit within the following words, running across the gap between them

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone helping out behind the counter of a delicatessen in Dubai.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an official or politician.

clue.text: Artful touches of nudism in film

indicators.note: artful suggests something cleverly arranged or crafted, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A tasteful art-house film with a few discreet nude scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the most wholesome film musical ever made is built from 'touches of nudism'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sound of Music is the 1965 musical film starring Julie Andrews as Maria.

clue.text: Check all others before shower

indicators.note: before places one part ahead of the next in this down entry

blocks.note: the rest means all the others
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect everything else before taking a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back, the same as to restrain it.

clue.text: Plant in small border

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an edge is a border or rim

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about something planted in a narrow flower border.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant that grows in wet ground.

clue.text: Batting crease about to be wiped as a precaution

indicators.note: wiping clears something away, so a short piece is removed from the word before it

blocks.note: a batsman who is batting is in
taken as written, before the cut
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning; these are the letters wiped

explanation.surface: A cricket groundsman clearing the batting crease ahead of bad weather, just to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the marked line where a batsman stands in cricket; 'about' is the short Latin-derived word used in business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in case is to do it as a safeguard against a possible event.

clue.text: Train in club on piece of gymnastic equipment

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: an iron is a type of golf club
the vaulting horse or pommel horse used in gymnastics

explanation.surface: A gymnast training with a club while balanced on the apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb about practising, but it is the noun, the locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old-fashioned, poetic name for a steam locomotive or railway train.

clue.text: Goes up with Conservative members

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
members in the sense of arms and legs

explanation.surface: Someone rises in the world by joining Tory party members.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend, so climbs is a present-tense equivalent of goes up.

clue.text: Chilean politician in Brazilian port on sub submerged in the drink?

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part on another sits above it and so comes first
something submerged is under the surface of a liquid, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Salvador is the port capital of Bahia state in Brazil
ale is a drink, here split open to take a filling
to sub someone is to lend them money

explanation.surface: A politician from Chile seen at a Brazilian harbour aboard a submarine that has gone under.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay as printed supplies only one of the two Ls in the surname; the question mark may excuse the looseness. To sub someone is British slang for lending them money.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Allende was the Marxist President of Chile from 1970 until the coup of 1973.

clue.text: In topping clothes?

blocks.note: surface reading: wearing smashing, terrific outfits
setter's reading: topping is slang for killing, so these are clothes worn for a murder

explanation.walkthrough: Topping is British slang both for 'excellent' and for 'killing'; the answer describes stunning clothes but literally means dressed for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for wearing very striking, glamorous clothes meant to impress.

clue.text: Man attached to the Spanish place of worship

indicators.note: attached to means joined on, so one part is fixed directly onto the next

blocks.note: a chap is a man
el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A man tied to a church in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a room set aside for prayer, so a place of worship.

clue.text: Arab fell in dock

blocks.note: first meaning: a North African of Arab and Berber descent
second meaning: an open upland, as a fell is in northern England
third meaning: to tie up a boat

explanation.surface: An Arab man collapsed on the quayside, or perhaps in the dock of a court.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two. 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall but is the northern English noun for a hill or high moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word is a historical name for a Muslim of North Africa, an open upland heath, and a verb for securing a vessel.

clue.text: TV programme - repeat - Coast?

blocks.note: an echo repeats a sound
the beach is where land meets sea

explanation.surface: A listings query: is this TV programme a repeat, and is it the one called Coast?
explanation.walkthrough: Coast is also the title of a BBC documentary series, which makes it look like a second programme name.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo Beach was a 2008 British TV drama set in a Cornish surfing town.

clue.text: Various priests press soldier about battle, initially

indicators.note: initially says the named piece comes at the start, ahead of the rest
turned about means facing the other way, so the two words before it are read backwards

blocks.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a 1914 battle
to iron clothes is to press them
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Several clergymen urge a soldier to talk about the battle he fought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a verb urging the soldier, but it is the household task. Mons was the British Army's first battle of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsignori is the Italian plural of monsignor, a title given to senior Roman Catholic priests.

clue.text: Spite shown by married woman

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
any woman's name will do; here Alice

explanation.surface: A wife behaving spitefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm others, and spite is a petty form of that ill will.

clue.text: Something requiring little thought in Reno, surprisingly goes without support

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not what was expected, so the letters come out in a new order
goes without is read as going outside, so the rearranged letters wrap around a word

blocks.note: the six letters reshuffled, to be split around the support
a bra is a support garment

explanation.surface: In Reno someone, to general surprise, does without a bra, and nobody thinks twice about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes without support' looks like going braless, but 'goes without' puts the jumbled letters outside BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is an informal term for a decision or task so easy it needs no thought.

clue.text: Shot captures Bond's boss leaving ceremony

indicators.note: to capture something is to take it in and hold it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a pop is a shot, as from a gun
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A gunman seizes James Bond's chief as he walks out of a formal event.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is splendid display and stately show, as in the phrase pomp and ceremony.

clue.text: Race officials set staggering charges

indicators.note: staggering means lurching unsteadily, so the word before it falls out of order

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
wards are people in someone's charge

explanation.surface: Racecourse officials impose astonishingly high fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' seems to describe the charges as huge, but it signals rearranging the word set.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are the officials who supervise a horse race and enforce its rules.

clue.text: City, very big in Asian country

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
OS is outsize, the clothing size

explanation.surface: A city that is huge by the standards of an Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked country in South-East Asia, between Vietnam and Thailand.

clue.text: Aim to get black, each one after being this

definitions.note: a cryptic description rather than a synonym: every ball in turn becomes this once it is aimed at

blocks.note: an aim is an object or goal
the black is the highest-scoring ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A snooker player lines up to pot the black, then each remaining ball in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose and cryptic: each ball on the table becomes the target in turn, the black included.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker or pool the object ball is the one the cue ball is aimed to strike.

clue.text: Everyone in base, except Tom, gets to vote

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so the name after it is taken away from the word before
in places one word inside another

blocks.note: the bottom is the base of something
taken as written; these letters are removed
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone at the base gets a say, except Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a person left out of the vote, but he is the tail end of a longer word for base.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a secret vote, the act of voting itself.

clue.text: Turn out once more - what did you say?

blocks.note: first meaning: to show up again, literally come a second time
second meaning: a request to repeat what was said

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a spoken phrase, so the definition text keeps its question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means to return or attend again, and idiomatically is a way of asking someone to repeat themselves.

clue.text: Plane crashes in Asian country

indicators.note: something that crashes is wrecked and broken up, so its letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: five letters of fodder

explanation.surface: News of an air disaster in a Himalayan state.
explanation.walkthrough: Nepal is notorious for air crashes in its mountains, so the surface is grimly realistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country in South Asia, between India and China.

clue.text: Austrian composer, a Lothario

blocks.note: first meaning: Hugo ..., the Austrian song composer
second meaning: a man who preys on women

explanation.surface: A Viennese composer with a reputation as a seducer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo Wolf wrote Lieder; a wolf is slang for a womaniser, as Lothario is the seducer in a Rowe play.

clue.text: Love Seve's finish

indicators.note: the finish of a name is its tail end, so only the closing letters are kept

blocks.note: Seve is the golfer Seve Ballesteros, and the end of his surname is kept

explanation.surface: Golfer Seve's love of a good finish on the 18th.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver must supply the full name Ballesteros and keep its last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, and the word stands for erotic love itself.

clue.text: Non-executive investor who keeps his mouth shut?

blocks.note: first meaning: a business backer who takes no part in running it
second meaning, playful: a companion who says nothing

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a joke on the literal sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A silent partner puts capital into a firm without managing it; read literally, the phrase is a companion who stays quiet.

clue.text: Ring in variegated crest of duck

indicators.note: in places the letter for a ring inside the other letters
variegated means patched with different colours, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters of crest reordered
O is the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: A ring around the multicoloured crest of a duck, as a birdwatcher might note.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck found in northern waters.

clue.text: Follows advice and pays attention

blocks.note: first meaning: heeds what is said
second meaning: concentrates on hearing something

explanation.surface: Someone takes the advice given and concentrates.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen can mean to heed and act on advice as well as to hear something attentively.
